$comment: Paste-ready values for the Muse Connector Platform form (https://muse.ai/platform → Submit a connector). Keys mirror the form's createConnectorSubmissionAction payload as observed on 2026-09-18. The icon is public/icon.png (512x512, ~12 KB). The three attestations are ticked in the form by the account owner.
useCases:
Search for class action settlements I might be eligible for based on the companies in my email receipts, and tell me which ones are worth filing.
Which open settlements need no proof of purchase and close in the next 30 days?
Go through my order emails from the last two years and check whether anything I bought has been recalled, and what refund I can get.
Check my credit cards for statement credits and perks I have not used this month, and remind me before they reset.
Are any of my airline miles or hotel points about to expire? What is the cheapest way to keep them alive?
Find all the places near me where I can get something free on my birthday, and tell me what to join and by when.
Every Monday, check whether any new settlements or recalls apply to me and only message me if there is something to do.
limits: Free, public and read-only. No account is required. U.S. settlements, recalls and rewards only. Rate limit 60 requests per minute per client (HTTP 429 with Retry-After beyond that). Results are informational: every item links to the official settlement site, CPSC notice, card issuer or brand page, and the connector never files claims, signs up for programs or makes purchases. Settlement data refreshes daily; recall data is a daily snapshot topped up live from the CPSC API; card, points and birthday catalogues carry a last-reviewed date and confidence rating per entry.
authOther: None required. Public read-only endpoint over streamable HTTP. An optional bearer API key can be enabled by the operator if Meta prefers keyed access for review.
extraNotes:
Dowser finds the money hiding in a person's life: open class action settlements matched to the brands they use, CPSC product recalls matched to things they own (with refund, replacement or repair remedies), unused credit card statement credits with reset dates, expiring airline and hotel points, and birthday freebies by state. It exists because the most-requested Muse tasks are money-recovery sweeps that are slow and brittle in a browser; Dowser turns them into one structured call and pairs naturally with Gmail receipts and Plaid transactions that Muse already has.

Technical notes for review:
- Hosted remote MCP server, Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST, stateless, JSON responses), built on the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Endpoint: /mcp. Server card: /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json.
- Six tools: search_settlements, match_recalls, card_benefits, points_expiry, birthday_freebies, check_for_new. All carry readOnlyHint: true, destructiveHint: false, idempotentHint: true. One prompt: find_my_money.
- REST mirror of every tool under /api/v1 with an OpenAPI 3.1 document at /openapi.json, for the Raw API path.
- No authentication required; no accounts; no personal data stored. Inputs are brand, product, card and program names, a U.S. state and a birthday month-day. Request logs are limited to hosting-provider metadata for rate limiting.
- Safety: the connector returns information and official links only. Filing a claim or joining a program happens in Muse's browser with the user's approval. Results include a disclaimer and source attribution (OpenClassActions.com and ClassAction.org are independent directories, not administrators; recall data is CPSC public data).
- Payments: none. Dowser does not sell anything.
- Test plan for end-to-end review: call search_settlements with brands ["Apple","Equifax"], match_recalls with products ["stroller","air fryer"], card_benefits with ["Amex Platinum"], birthday_freebies with state "TX". All return within two seconds with official links.
- Open source: https://github.com/harris-ryder/dowser
